issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be rejected under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure when its averments, read meaningfully with the documents relied upon, show that the suit is barred by limitation, even if limitation is generally a mixed question of law and fact.

The limitation period for challenging registered instruments runs from registration, which gives constructive notice, and cannot be extended by pleading a later date of actual knowledge that is illusory.

A claim for declaratory relief challenging a voidable transfer must be brought within the applicable limitation period, including within three years after a minor attains majority where the right to sue is treated as accruing then.
A claim for possession of immovable property based on title is barred when it is not brought within the twelve-year period prescribed by Article 65 of the Limitation Act.

A stranger to a compromise decree cannot institute a separate suit to set it aside because Order XXIII Rule 3A of the Code of Civil Procedure bars such a suit, and the challenge must be brought before the court that recorded the compromise.
A person who is a stranger to property cannot obtain an injunction restraining its owners from dealing with it when the consequential title claim is barred.
